transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve been feeling like the best part of my life is behind me. Not dramatically, just… in a quiet way that doesn’t really let up. It feels like no matter how much I plan or try to be disciplined, I can’t quite get back to feeling like myself.
How long have you been feeling this way?
A little over three years now… since I hurt myself hiking. About three years and three months, I guess.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like before the accident?
I’m not sure. Some things are still… okay, I guess. I don’t know that I enjoy them the way I used to, but it’s hard to say.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities you used to find pleasurable?
I don’t know if I’d put it that strongly. I still do some things… they just don’t feel the same, maybe. It’s hard for me to tell.
Do you feel like you've lost pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?
I’m not sure, honestly. Maybe some, but… I still do a few things. I just don’t really know if I’d call it pleasure or not.
Do you often feel sad?
Most days, I wouldn’t say I’m crying or anything like that. It’s more just… a kind of gray feeling underneath things, even when I’m doing something or sitting with my wife.
Are there things that you used to find pleasurable but no longer do?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed one specific thing where I’d say, “I don’t enjoy that anymore.” It’s more… hard to pin down.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in social activities or being around other people?
Some, I guess. I still handle things at home, but I don’t go out as much. I’ve backed away from mentoring, community events… music get-togethers. Travel plans too. My weeks are just smaller now.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight since you started feeling this way?
No, not that I’ve really noticed. My weight seems about the same, as far as I can tell.
Do you ever think about death?
Not really... I don’t think about it much. I mean, not in any particular way.
Have you ever had a period of two weeks or more where you felt consistently depressed?

Yes… I suppose so. It’s not like I’m crying all the time or anything dramatic. It’s more like most days there’s this low, gray feeling underneath things, even when I’m in the studio or just having dinner with my wife.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities that normally would bring you happiness?
I’m not sure I’d put it that strongly. I still enjoy some things, I think… maybe just not with the same ease as before. It’s hard to say.
Do you feel like you're unable to find pleasure in almost all activities?
Almost all? No… I don’t think I’d say that. Some things still feel okay, just maybe not as much as they used to.
How long do these periods of feeling down or gray usually last?
It’s been… a while. Since the hiking injury, really. A little over three years now—about three years and a few months.
Have you had more than two periods of feeling this low, gray feeling in the past?

It’s not really separate periods, I guess. Most days it’s just… there. Not dramatic, not like I’m crying all the time—more like a gray feeling underneath things, even when I’m doing something in the studio or having dinner with my wife.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from almost all activities most of the time?
No, I wouldn’t say almost all activities. It’s more… muted sometimes, but I can still enjoy some things.
Do you feel like you have to push yourself to do things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… sometimes. I still do things—shopping, little projects around the house—but I have to sort of push myself to get started. Even setting up for a mentoring session, or walking around a community event, can leave me more worn out than it seems like it should. A nap doesn’t really clear it.
Have you lost or gained a significant amount of weight since you started feeling this way?
Not really. I mean, my weight’s moved around a little, but nothing I’d call significant.
Has this low, gray feeling you've described been continuous since the hiking injury, or have you had periods where it significantly improved?
It’s been pretty much there since the hiking injury. A little over three years now… maybe three years and three months. I wouldn’t say it really lifted for any long stretch.
Do you usually feel this low, gray feeling for most of the day?

Most days, yes. It’s not like I’m crying all day or anything… it’s just this low, gray feeling underneath things, even when I’m doing something normal like being in the studio or having dinner with my wife.
